w10_T4_004832: A weaving workshop finished 240 scarves in each of the 7 months of its winter season. It also had 80 scarves left over from the previous year stacked in the store cupboard, and these were counted with the rest. Every single scarf in that pile had been made from 6 skeins of wool. The workshop measures its yarn in metres rather than in kilometres. Of all the skeins needed, 6070 came free from the village co-op and the workshop had to buy the remainder. How many skeins did the workshop have to buy?
w10_T4_004836: A research greenhouse started the trial with 202 seed trays, and every tray was cut down the middle into 2 half trays. Each half tray was then filled with 7 germination pods. The greenhouse is 18 metres wide. Jonas carried in 54 spare pods from the shed, and Mira brought 77 pods, rather more than Jonas had found. A technician later discovered 9 further pods on a bench and added them. During planting week 2585 pods were taken out to the field beds. How many pods were still in the greenhouse afterwards?
w10_T4_004839: Marek began the month with 77 bus tokens in his wallet, and his route passes 14 stops on the way to work. Commuting used up 66 of the tokens, and he gave 8 of them to a visiting friend. He took what was left to the transport office, where each token was converted into 7 ride credits. He then spent 20 of those credits travelling at the weekend. The office upgraded every credit he still held into 6 bonus credits, and he used 5 of the bonus credits on the Monday after. How many credits does Marek have now?
w10_T4_004840: The Hillcrest library had 217 films on its DVD rack on Monday morning, and it logs its loan periods in days rather than in weeks. On Monday members borrowed 31 of them. On Tuesday 45 discs came back and went straight onto the rack. On Wednesday another 30 were borrowed, and on Thursday 30 discs were returned to the rack. A dozen children signed up for the summer reading club that week. How many films were on the rack when the library opened on Friday?
w10_T4_004841: A river hatchery keeps its young trout in 227 identical tanks, with 5 fingerlings in every tank. Half of the hatchery staff work at the weekend. Over the first cold month 183 of the fingerlings did not survive. A neighbouring hatchery then donated 24 healthy fingerlings, which joined the same tanks. At feeding time each fish in the hatchery is given 4 pellets. How many pellets does one feeding round use?
w10_T4_004842: Ines had 182 photographs in her shoebox before the exhibition. She had 45 more prints made and dropped them into the same box. She gave 141 of the photographs to the families who appear in them, and 8 more were spoiled when a window was left open in the rain. She spread what remained equally across 6 display boards, then hung only one of those boards in the hall and stored the rest. A dozen visitors came to the opening. Every photograph on the hall board was held up with 8 brass tacks. How many tacks were used on the hall board?
w10_T4_004843: Aiko opened the plant in the morning with 164 sealed cases in the loading bay, and every case contained 9 component trays. Each of those trays was packed with 7 memory chips. Her colleague Bram arrived before lunch with 26 loose chips from the test bench, and they were counted in with the others. During the afternoon the buyer valued every chip at 5 credits. In the evening the accounts office converted each credit into 8 supplier points. The points were then split equally among the 5 production teams. How many points went to the team Aiko leads?
w10_T4_004844: The Carfax Museum counted 130 visitors through its doors before ten o'clock. Another 59 came in during the late morning. The lunchtime hour brought a further 79 people, and 33 more arrived in the middle of the afternoon. The museum has 12 galleries spread over two wings. In the evening, during the late opening, 62 visitors came through. How many visitors did the museum have that day?
w10_T4_004845: Rosa had 92 balls of wool stacked in her workroom basket. She used up 61 of them finishing a coat for her neighbour. From every ball she still had she knitted 9 patchwork squares. Her aunt posted her 38 finished squares to add to the pile. She then sewed 222 of the squares into a blanket that was given to the village hall. Each square that remained was decorated with 5 wooden buttons, and she counted these together with the 62 loose buttons already sitting in her tin. How many buttons did she count in total?
w10_T4_004851: A small plant shop had 38 potted cacti on its stands at the start of the fair, and it opens 5 days a week. During the fair 36 of the cacti were sold to visitors. On the Monday afterwards a grower delivered 28 new cacti to the shop. The owner divided all the cacti equally across 3 shelves, kept the window shelf in the shop and sent the other shelves to a sister branch. That spring every cactus on the window shelf opened 6 flowers. How many flowers opened on the window shelf?
w10_T4_004854: The school canteen had 198 bread rolls in its warm cabinet at the start of the day, and the kitchen weighs its flour in grams rather than in kilograms. Breakfast service took 84 rolls out of the cabinet. A delivery van brought 10 rolls mid-morning, and the baker pulled 66 more out of the oven before noon. Every roll was then sliced into 3 pieces for the sandwich bar, tripling the count on the counter. Lunch service used 468 of those pieces, and 45 untouched pieces came back from the staff room afterwards. The canteen seats 240 pupils. How many pieces were left at the end of the day?
w10_T4_004869: The Larkhill apiary kept 169 hives on the hillside last spring, and the farm around it covers 40 hectares. A pollination contract moved 151 of those hives to an orchard fifty miles away for the whole season. Every hive that stayed on the hillside holds 7 wooden frames. Each frame carries 9 separate combs of honey. When the combs were spun, each one filled 9 jars. The store room already held 9 jars from the previous autumn, and they were counted with the new ones. How many jars were in the store room?
w10_T4_004870: The lemonade stall began the fair morning with 155 crates in its trailer, and a friend wheeled over 6 more crates before the gates opened. A dozen helpers took turns behind the counter. Every crate on the trailer held 8 bottles, and the stall lists its prices in cents rather than in dollars. Before noon 506 bottles were sold. Just after midday 26 unopened bottles were returned by a school group. Through the afternoon a further 678 bottles were sold, and in the evening 62 bottles came back unsold from the second counter. How many bottles did the stall still have at closing time?
w10_T4_004872: Yuki folded 58 paper cranes during the first week of the memorial project. She sent 30 of them to the children's hospital straight away. Her whole class then joined in, and the number of cranes she held tripled, becoming 3 times what she had. A friend from another school posted her 61 more cranes. When the display went up, volunteers folded a matching crane for every one Yuki had, so the display held twice as many. Each crane on the display was hung on a thread with 4 glass beads. How many beads were used on the display?
w10_T4_004877: Malik baked 29 lemon cupcakes for the weekend. His sister Zara took 10 of them to her football practice. The family ate 8 more at supper on Friday. On Saturday Malik gave 5 cupcakes to the neighbours who had helped him move a wardrobe. On Sunday morning 3 cupcakes went into the lunchboxes for the week. Every cupcake still on the rack was then cut into 4 small pieces for a tasting plate. How many pieces were on the tasting plate?
w10_T4_004885: Ana picked 14 tomatoes from her allotment on Saturday morning and 4 more from the same plants that afternoon. Her neighbour Piet, whose greenhouse had done far better than her plot, handed her 31 of his tomatoes over the fence. Ana cooked 39 of the tomatoes into sauce for the freezer. From each tomato that was left she saved 7 seeds for the next season. When she tested the saved seeds, 56 of them were hollow and she threw those away. How many seeds did Ana keep?
w10_T4_004889: A theatre printed 221 programmes for each of the 2 opening nights, so the print run was double the single-night figure. Ushers handed out 313 programmes over those two nights. A stagehand then found 50 unopened programmes in a props box and added them to the pile. The theatre has 18 rows in the stalls, and the box office records running times in minutes rather than in hours. For the tour the printer produced triple the surviving pile, making 3 copies of every programme. Later 235 of those copies were sent for recycling. How many programmes remained?
w10_T4_004891: A hillside vineyard tends 204 vines along its lower terrace, and this year every vine carried 6 bunches of grapes. The grower added 40 bunches from the old row by the wall, 60 bunches from the upper terrace, and 11 bunches from the trellis beside the house. Each bunch was pressed into 9 measures of juice. A winery in the valley bought 7734 measures and took them away in a tanker. How many measures of juice did the vineyard keep?
w10_T4_004893: Sofia had 68 sticker sheets, and every sheet carried 6 stickers. She and her cousin Luis shared all the stickers equally between 4 boxes, and Sofia took just one box home while the other boxes stayed at his house. The arcade in town is open 11 hours a day. There, each sticker in her box was exchanged for 9 game tokens. A weekend promotion then tripled her tokens, giving her 3 times as many. She spent 92 tokens on the racing machine, and every token she had left was later converted into 9 loyalty points. How many loyalty points did Sofia end up with?
w10_T4_004895: A county archive stores its atlases on 85 long shelves, with 9 atlases standing on each shelf. Half of those shelves are down in the basement, and the archive records the age of a document in months rather than in years. Every atlas in the building contains 4 fold-out maps. A survey found that 706 of the maps were too badly foxed to keep, and they were withdrawn. A partner archive in the next county then borrowed 428 of the remaining maps for an exhibition. How many maps were still held in the county archive?
w10_T4_004896: Priyanka set out 123 paper cups at the halfway water station of a road race. Her fellow volunteer Noor brought 20 more cups from the gazebo, and the supply van dropped off 61 additional cups. The race itself is 42 kilometres long. A gust of wind blew 19 cups off the table and they had to be binned. Every cup on the table was used twice during the race, so 2 servings were poured from each one. Each serving was given 5 ice cubes, and the cooler still held 47 spare cubes that were counted in as well. How many ice cubes were counted at the station?
w10_T4_004903: Jonah had 94 coins saved in a jar on his windowsill. His grandmother gave him 42 coins for his birthday, and he earned 26 more coins doing jobs around the house. Half of his friends keep savings jars too. He then spent 152 coins on a second-hand board game at the market. Clearing out the sofa the next weekend, he found 6 coins and dropped them into the jar. How many coins were in Jonah's jar afterwards?
w10_T4_004904: Mateo spent the morning at the cannery loading 43 pallets, and every pallet took 8 cartons. Each carton in the warehouse is packed with 9 tins of beans. The plant employs 76 people across its two shifts. At midday his colleague Rina wheeled in 58 loose tins from the repacking line and they joined the count. In the evening the sales office valued every tin in the warehouse at 5 koruna. What was the total value in koruna of the tins in the warehouse?
w10_T4_004907: A cycling club logs each rider's training time, and the coach writes every total in minutes rather than in hours. Half the members also ride at the weekend. Elif recorded 13 minutes on Monday, when heavy rain cut her ride short. She rode for 72 minutes on Tuesday and 19 minutes on Wednesday. On Thursday she managed 30 minutes before dark, and on Friday she rode for 67 minutes. How many minutes did Elif record for the week?
w10_T4_004911: A stationery shop had 225 pencils in its drawer at the start of the term, and it measures pencil leads in millimetres rather than in centimetres. A wholesaler delivered 49 more pencils in the first week. Over the term 247 pencils were sold to students. For the new term the owner decided to order 5 replacement pencils for every pencil still sitting in the drawer. The supplier already had 16 pencils on back order for the shop, and those were added to the same order. How many pencils were on the order in total?
